research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10920 (26 FR 1463, PDF pages 3-3; Federal Register issue of February 21, 1961; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10920.txt), headed Executive Order 10920, signed by John F. Kennedy on February 18, 1961. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Revoking Executive Order No. 10700 of February 25, 1957, as amended (Operations Coordinating Board)). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: the order has one operative sentence, the revocation of Executive Order No. 10700 of February 25, 1957, as amended, which provided further for the Operations Coordinating Board. The dossier's one clause for this number is another order's text: the registered text file prints Executive Order 10919 (an emergency board for Pan American World Airways) ahead of this order on the same Register page, and the dossier clause runs across the 10919 text. I therefore correct the inventory to one clause, the operative sentence of Executive Order 10920 itself, as stated in the inventory reason. The order states no effective date, so it took effect when signed on February 18, 1961; the Federal Register printed it on February 21, 1961, which is the alternative date a reader might take for effectiveness. The revocation is a single act that the order performs by its own words when it issues; once made it commands nothing further, so the clause is exhausted by performance on the signing date. What survives is the fact that the revoked order no longer operates, which is a consequence of the act and not a continuing command of this order. The three chosen machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes plus operative sentences of 17521 saved order texts) each state their coverage with no warning; their coverage notes were read. They search by this order's number, and none returned a hit for it.
